classification: Retrospective read-only forensic replay of an already observed Team Flare treatment; not a new prospective benchmark and not eligible for win-rate inference.
intervention: No decision or policy change. Reuse the existing generic both-seat Team Flare prompt resolver and the exact v2 single-root Team Flare treatment; add passive actual Store AttackAction/DealDamageEffect/PutCountersEffect/KnockOutEffect observation and independent owner Prize-to-hand custody observation.

questions.attackDamage: Record every actual opponent Energy Drive damage effect and the target Active's public damage before/after.
questions.knockout: Record actual native KnockOutEffect victim, damage, Prize entitlement and turn.
questions.prizeCustody: Record the actual ChoosePrizePrompt owner, selected physical Prize-card count, native resolution and transfer into the owner's hand.
questions.promotion: Record the actual ChoosePokemonPrompt and promoted Active after the KO chain.
questions.repeatability: Require exact A versus ARepeat target attack-observation tape and preserve all 24 native attempts.

limitations: The underlying v7 cohort was chosen retrospectively after observing the target hand and root.
The generic prompt v1 handler is used only to reproduce the already known single Team Flare root; the target decision is not prospective.
The Store effect observer is read-only and records engine effects, not a complete independent paper-rules certificate.
The Prize observer proves physical owner-hand custody for matched Prize prompts, not the origin of every KnockOutEffect.
The original A/B/A cohort has zero native terminal games and zero paper-qualified competitive games.
The opponent policy remains weak and is not an adversarially validated player.
No official 25-minute paper clock is modeled.
